Which Weather Model Is Most Accurate? We Score Them Every Day, in the Open

Community Article Published
November 13, 2026 Upvote 11 VIDRAFT_LAB SeaWolf-AI FINAL-Bench

A forecast that is one degree closer, or one day earlier, changes real decisions. A farmer decides when to harvest. A grid operator decides how much power to buy. An airline decides which flights to hold. A city decides whether to open its shelters. Weather prediction is one of the few fields where accuracy, science and economic value meet in the same number.
That is why we built two things and released both on Hugging Face:

Darwin-Prediction-Weather, VIDRAFT's weather prediction system.
Global Weather Model Leaderboard, a public board that scores the world's forecast models against what actually happened, every day.

The question: AI or physics?

For decades, weather forecasts have come from physics models that solve the equations of the atmosphere on supercomputers. In the last three years a new generation of AI models has arrived, trained on historical weather. Both kinds now run side by side at the world's weather centres.
Which one should you trust for tomorrow, for three days ahead, for a week ahead? Published papers answer this for past years. We wanted the answer for this year, updated daily, with the data open for anyone to check.

How the leaderboard works

Every day the board records what each model predicted for 24 cities on six continents, up to 10 days ahead. When the observed value for a day is published, every forecast made for that day is scored, and the cumulative record is updated.

Item
Rule

Models
ECMWF IFS and AIFS, NOAA GFS and AIGFS, DWD ICON, JMA GSM, ECCC GEM, MET Norway, and Darwin-Prediction-Weather

Elements
Daily maximum temperature, daily minimum temperature, daily maximum wind speed, daily precipitation total

Truth
ERA5 reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Change Service

Score
Root-mean-square error. Lower is better

Fairness
Every model is scored on the same cases: days and cities where all listed models issued a forecast

Record
From 1 January 2026, updated once a day

Each model carries its developer, its country and its type, AI or Physics (Supercomputer), and links to its official page.

What the 2026 record shows

Two findings stand out in the record so far.
First, AI models now lead. Among the models of the national and international weather centres, ECMWF's AI model AIFS has lower error than ECMWF's physics model IFS at every lead time, and NOAA's AIGFS has lower error than NOAA's GFS at every lead time.
Second, fusion goes further. Darwin-Prediction-Weather has the lowest error in all four elements, at every lead time from 1 to 7 days.

Four elements, four tabs

Temperature is only part of the weather. The board gives each element its own tab, with the same panels: champion, accuracy board, error by forecast day, city map, daily results and monthly champions.

Who wins where

A single global number hides a lot. The board breaks the record down by period, by lead time and by city, so you can see who wins where.

Yesterday's result, today, and the next ten days

For every city, the board lays out a rolling timeline: the last seven days with the actual value and the model that came closest, today so far, and the forecast for the next ten days. Each morning the timeline moves one day to the left. Yesterday's forecast becomes today's result, and it is scored.

Live Earth

One button opens live global maps of wind, clouds, rain radar and temperature, and a satellite map that shows the champion of each city over live rain radar.

How Darwin-Prediction-Weather works

Darwin is VIDRAFT's family of models built on one idea: combine the strengths of several strong models into one that is stronger than any of them. Darwin-Prediction-Weather applies that idea to the atmosphere.

Forecast engine. It produces a single forecast by skill-weighted fusion of global forecasts, with local correction for temperature and wind. It learns only from days whose observed value was already known before the forecast it is scored on. Nothing from the future enters.
Decision core. A Darwin-27B model with a calibrated readout turns forecast fields into decisions: go or no-go, threshold exceedance, category probabilities.

The same engine was also evaluated on WeatherBench 2, the standard benchmark for AI weather models run by Google Research. On the 2020 deterministic protocol it records the lowest error in all 15 evaluated cells (2 m temperature, 500 hPa geopotential and 850 hPa temperature at 1, 3, 5, 7 and 10 days). The forecast files are public and the entry has been submitted to the WeatherBench 2 team.

Everything is open to check

The board: https://huggingface.co/spaces/FINAL-Bench/Weather-Model-Leaderboard
The daily record of every forecast and every observed value since 2026-01-01, as CSV: Weather-Model-Forecast-Archive
The model: Darwin-Prediction-Weather
WeatherBench 2 forecast files: Darwin-Prediction-Weather-WB2

Direct links open a specific view. For example, the precipitation tab: https://huggingface.co/spaces/FINAL-Bench/Weather-Model-Leaderboard#el=precip

What comes next

Forecasts 8 to 10 days ahead enter the ranking as their target days are verified.
Scoring against station observations, alongside ERA5.
More cities and more elements.
A forecasting game on Hugging Face where anyone can test their own forecast against the models.

Better forecasts come from comparison in the open. We welcome questions, corrections and new models to add.
